paragraphs: This flow walks through everything the Post for Me API can do when connecting a social account, so you can see the full range in one place.
When you're building your own UI, you'll likely want some of these configurations pre-determined so your users see a simpler action.
To help you get started, we've crafted a set of drop-in UI components you can build from.

description.instagram: Sends the user to Instagram to log in and authorize the connection directly.
description.facebook: Sends the user to Facebook, where they pick the linked Instagram account to connect.

linkedin.label: Connection type
linkedin.education: This selects which LinkedIn API Post for Me uses — not the type of account you're connecting. Organization is recommended: it unlocks the most capabilities, including posting on behalf of users.

tiktok.label: API
tiktok.education: TikTok offers two APIs. Business API is recommended — it connects and posts just like Standard, but adds expanded post analytics and looser rate limits. Despite the name it isn't limited to business accounts; it's simply the more advanced of the two.

x.label: API version
x.education: X offers two OAuth versions. OAuth 2.0 is recommended — it's the current standard and what new developer apps are issued, with access tokens that refresh automatically in the background. OAuth 1.0a is the legacy flow; its tokens never expire, so it's worth keeping only if you already have accounts connected through it.

bluesky.education: Use an app password, not your main Bluesky password. Create one in Bluesky → Settings → App Passwords.

feeds.label: Feed & analytics
feeds.help: Read the account's posts and metrics.

externalId.label: External ID
externalId.help: Your own identifier for this account. It's returned on the connected account so you can match it back to your user.

New accounts won't be able to connect, accounts already connected will stop working, and any scheduled posts to {{platform}} will fail. You can set it up again later, but every account will need to reconnect.
platforms.disableQuickstartConfirmBody: This turns {{platform}} off for this project. New accounts won't be able to connect, accounts already connected will stop working, and any scheduled posts to {{platform}} will fail. You can turn it back on later, but every account will need to reconnect.
platforms.noKeysBody: {{platform}} is enabled and ready. Account owners sign in with their own handle and app password, so there's no developer app to register and nothing to configure here.

variants.instagram: Users sign in on Instagram itself. Works with any professional account and needs no linked Facebook Page — the shortest path for most people.
variants.instagramWFacebook: Users sign in on Facebook and pick a linked Instagram account. Requires a Facebook developer app and an account linked to a Page.
variants.tiktokBusiness: The same connection and posting experience as Standard, plus expanded post analytics and looser rate limits. Despite the name, it isn't restricted to business accounts.
variants.tiktokStandard: Where most projects start, and the more limited of the two: tighter rate limits and fewer analytics.
variants.xOauth2: X's current standard, and what new developer apps are issued. Posts text and media exactly like OAuth 1.0a; access tokens refresh in the background.
variants.xOauth1: The legacy flow. Posts the same, but its tokens never expire — so connections keep working without any refresh.

platforms.sharedCredsBody: {{platform}} is enabled and runs on Post for Me's shared credentials, so there's nothing else to set up here.
platforms.sharedCredsPendingBody: {{platform}} runs on Post for Me's shared credentials, so enabling it is the only setup it needs.
platforms.noKeysPendingBody: {{platform}} has no developer app to register — account owners sign in with their own handle and app password. Enabling it is the only setup it needs.

instagram.title: Start with Instagram Login
instagram.body: Users sign in on Instagram itself. There is no Facebook app to register and no Page to link, so it is the fastest route to a working connection — for you and for them.

instagram.title: Add Facebook Login to widen who can connect
instagram.body: With both on, each user picks their own route — which helps people who run Instagram from a linked Facebook Page. It costs more setup on your side: a second developer app to register and configure, and those users need a Page already linked to their account.

tiktok.title: Start with the Business API
tiktok.body: It connects and posts exactly like the Standard API — nothing changes for your users — but you get expanded analytics on every post and far looser rate limits. The name is misleading: it isn't restricted to business accounts. Treat it as the advanced version of Standard rather than a different product.

tiktok.title: Standard API is the more limited option
tiktok.body: It's the usual starting point and it posts perfectly well, but rate limits are tighter and there's much less analytics data to read back. Choose it only if Business API access isn't available to you.

x.title: Start with OAuth 2.0
x.body: It's the current X standard and posts text and media exactly like OAuth 1.0a, so nothing changes for the people connecting. Access tokens are refreshed for you in the background.

x.title: OAuth 1.0a trades modern for durable
x.body: Its tokens never expire, so a connection can't lapse and needs no refresh. Worth keeping on if you already have accounts connected through it.

x.title: Turning on both changes your API calls
x.body: With both configured, createAuthURL must say which to use — pass connection_type as "oauth1" or "oauth2". Omitting it returns an error, so only enable both if your integration sets it.

platforms.credentialsChangeBody: Accounts connected with the current credentials will stop working and must reconnect before they can post again. Any scheduled posts from those accounts will fail until they do.
